title: Volatility-adjusted position sizing
summary: Set the stop from the market's movement, such as 2 × ATR, then size = money at risk ÷ (stop distance × value per unit). The loss at the stop stays the same.
unreliableWhen: ATR describes the past and can be low just before a jump. Gaps and slippage can push a loss past the stop. Some markets cannot be sized small enough, so the answer is to skip.
goodExample: Two stocks at 40.00: ATR 0.80 gives 62 shares and ATR 2.00 gives 25 shares, both risking about 100 USD.
badExample: Keeping the same size when ATR doubles, so the loss at the stop doubles too.

chart.lookFor: Read ATR 14 at the start and end of the chart. Work out a 2 × ATR stop and the size for the same money at risk at each point.
